page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering a balanced resource profile for routine computing workloads. It is equipped with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores and 8 threads from an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, maintaining an even 4.0 GB ratio per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, relying on remote network storage for disk operations.

Empirical benchmark results demonstrate mixed compute and throughput metrics. The instance achieves strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng at 2683.18, alongside a multi-core score of 10751.22. However, single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores settle in lower tiers at 905.0 and 3520.0 respectively, with software compilation scoring 5099.0 and text processing at 1167.0. Data compression tasks show modest results, with single-threaded gzip processing 18.9 GB/sec. Conversely, memory bandwidth remains steady for large uncached operations at 44.99 GB/sec read and 31.82 GB/sec write. In simulated enterprise tests, PassMark CPU reaches 11750.5, while PassMark database operations record 3246.96 and Redis SET reaches 8.42 million operations per second.

From an architectural perspective, e2-standard-8 provides a cost-efficient middle-tier configuration where heavy GPU processing or extreme single-threaded burst capability is not required. Static web serving throughput reaches 7.58 GB/sec, making it well matched for standard web serving, microservice hosting, routine database operations, and lightweight backend tasks. Compute-heavy workloads such as dense vector processing or extensive data compression will face throughput limitations given the absence of AVX-512 extensions and modest compression benchmark ratings.

It features 16 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX, AES, and BMI2 instruction support, while lacking bundled local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments position the instance in the middle tier across standard operational metrics, generating 8.42 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark CPU score of 11750.5, and static web serving throughput of 7.58 GB/sec. While stress-ng reflects strong single-core performance, synthetic tests like Geekbench and decompression benchmarks demonstrate modest throughput under compute-dense routines. Offering balanced compute and memory capacity, the instance delivers predictable resource allocation for general-purpose application hosting, standard web servers, intermediate database workloads, and microservice infrastructure.
